artists.biography:
Jean Michel André Jarre (born 24 August 1948 in Lyon) is a French composer, performer and music producer. He is a pioneer in the electronic, ambient and New Age genres, and known as an organiser of outdoor spectacles of his music featuring lights, laser displays, and fireworks.

Jarre was raised in Lyon by his mother and grandparents, and trained on the piano. From an early age he was introduced to a variety of art forms, including those of street performers, jazz musicians, and the artist Pierre Soulages. He played guitar in a band, but his musical style was perhaps most heavily influenced by Pierre Schaeffer, a pioneer of musique concrète at the Groupe de Recherches Musicales.

His first mainstream success was the 1976 album Oxygène. Recorded in a makeshift studio at his home, the album sold an estimated 12 million copies. Oxygène was followed in 1978 by Équinoxe, and in 1979 Jarre performed to a record-breaking audience of more than a million people at the Place de la Concorde, a record he has since broken three times. More albums were to follow, but his 1979 concert served as a blueprint for his future performances around the world. Several of his albums have been released to coincide with large-scale outdoor events, and he is now perhaps as well known as a performer as a musician.

As of 2004 Jarre had sold an estimated 80 million albums. He was the first Western musician to be allowed to perform in the People's Republic of China, and holds the world record for the largest-ever audience at an outdoor event.

perplexity.description:
Equinoxe is the fourth studio album by Jean-Michel Jarre, released in November 1978 on Disques Dreyfus. Following the massive success of his 1976 breakthrough Oxygène, the album continues Jarre's exploration of electronic music with a cohesive suite of eight instrumental pieces titled Equinoxe Part 1 through Part 8. The album's thematic foundation centers on the relationship between humanity and nature within an increasingly technological world, with the parts flowing seamlessly into one another to create a unified listening experience.

Musically, Equinoxe is characterized by layered analog synthesizers, rhythmic patterns, and melodic development that builds dynamically throughout the suite. The production creates a hypnotic, atmospheric soundscape with futuristic and extraterrestrial qualities, establishing Jarre's signature approach to electronic composition. The first single, Part 5, achieved significant commercial success, followed by Part 4 as a second single.

The album's commercial performance was exceptional. It achieved Gold status upon release and accumulated over 500,000 sales by early July 1979, remaining in the French Top 10 throughout the summer. The release was further bolstered by a landmark outdoor concert at Place de la Concorde in Paris on July 14, 1979, which drew approximately one million attendees, dramatically increasing album sales. A package combining Equinoxe with the reissued Oxygène proved particularly successful, with the label shipping 800,000 units of Jarre albums within six weeks. Estimates place total sales at approximately 1.35 million copies by the present day, establishing Equinoxe as one of France's best-selling albums ever.
